description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, and this program does not view a transaction - it ADDS one. app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 reads 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the project's own online inventory corroborates it independently: README.md:224 records CT02 COTRN02 COTRN02C as Transaction Add against README.md:223, which records CT01 COTRN01 COTRN01C as Transaction View - the inverse of the prompt's mapping, whose viewing half is parity/COTRN01C. Rule R1 resolves it: the name is taken from the prompt verbatim and the behaviour from the source. Practice B4 requires the swap to be recorded here rather than quietly repaired, because a reader who trusts the class name writes a read-only expectation, and a read-only expectation passes against a program that inserts nothing. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only on that account. One citation correction, per practice B8: earlier cases in this folder cite README.md:222 for the CT02 row, but the verified line is 224 - identical in the pristine Initial Commit, in the setup commit and in the working tree, none of which differ in README.md - and it sits inside the L213-231 inventory range. PROVENANCE, PRACTICE B12: every expected value below was derived statically, by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl and app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and cross-checking them against the xxxI widths app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY declares and the real fixture data under app/data/ASCII. Not one value was captured from a live COBOL run, and none could have been: AAP 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers - no z/OS runtime, a GnuCOBOL whose indexed file handler is disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot produce an executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no installable alternative compiler - which make executing the 28 legacy programs impossible in this environment. That is risk R-A: the provenance of the expected values changes and nothing else does. The 20 cases per program, the field-by-field diffing and the requirement that the diff count reach zero across all twenty all stand (gates G15 and G18). WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: re-entry, the RECEIVE, and arm five of the five-arm EVALUATE EIBAID. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1', so CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is already true when :120 tests it, control takes the ELSE at :131, and :132 performs RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN before :133 evaluates EIBAID. This case is the folder's primary proof of gate G30, which is the rule that EVALUATE is ordered: the first matching WHEN wins, and WHEN OTHER is the default and must be last. The five arms in source order are (1) DFHENTER at :134, PERFORM PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, owned by cases 06 through 20; (2) DFHPF3 at :136, the CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM guard at :137-142 and then RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN at :143, owned by case03; (3) DFHPF4 at :144, PERFORM CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN, owned by case04; (4) DFHPF5 at :146, PERFORM COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA, documented in case20; and (5) WHEN OTHER at :148, which is this case - :149 raises WS-ERR-FLG, :150 moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into WS-MESSAGE and :151 performs SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN. THE AID CHOSEN IS DFHPF6, and it matches none of arms one to four: this program names exactly four attention identifiers - DFHENTER at :134, DFHPF3 at :136, DFHPF4 at :144 and DFHPF5 at :146 - and PF6 is none of them, so the EVALUATE can only reach it by falling through all four. It was chosen over any other unnamed key because it is the immediate successor of the LAST named arm at every indirection the translation makes: in arm order PF5 then PF6, in EBCDIC byte value 0xF5 then 0xF6, and in token order PFK05 then PFK06. It is therefore the first key that an arm list one entry too long, or a range test such as PF3 through PF6, would wrongly capture, which makes it the sharpest available evidence that the named set genuinely stops at PF5. case06 pairs with it by reaching the same arm with DFHPF12, which is 0x7C and nowhere near the named block, so the two together show the default arm catching both a byte-adjacent unnamed key and a distant one. The key is declared by mnemonic and resolved through common.CicsAid rather than written as a raw byte, because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository - risk R-D - and CicsAid is its single reproduction, taken from IBM CICS documentation. One trap is worth naming: CicsAid's PF13 to PF24 mnemonics would NOT serve here, because common.PfKeyResolver faithfully reproduces the fold app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy applies at its L54-77, so DFHPF15 resolves to PFK03 and would reach arm two rather than arm five. THE MESSAGE, BYTE FOR BYTE: app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY as PIC X(50) with the value 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' followed by nine spaces - forty-nine written characters, which the PIC X(50) field pads to fifty. :150 moves that fifty-byte field into WS-MESSAGE, which app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:38 declares PIC X(80), left justified and space padded to eighty. :520 then moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO, which app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY:144 declares PIC X(78). Naming the direction explicitly, per practice B8 and rule R5: the sender is WIDER than the receiver, so this is a truncating alphanumeric move, and COBOL truncates PIC X on the RIGHT, dropping the final two bytes of WS-MESSAGE. Both dropped bytes are spaces, so no visible text is lost and ERRMSGO holds the forty characters of message followed by thirty-eight spaces. Both images are pinned, at eighty and seventy-eight bytes, on the WS_MESSAGE_80 and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channels in that order. NO FIELD HIGHLIGHT AND NO CURSOR MOVE, WHICH IS THE HALF OF GATE G38 MOST EASILY GOT WRONG. This is a re-entry case and it does set the error flag at :149, but the arm applies no field attribute and moves no -1 to any xxxL item, so cursorField is null and no highlight is expected anywhere. The contrast is in the source rather than in an opinion: the NOTFND arm of READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :591-596 moves -1 TO ACTIDINL OF COTRN2AI before it sends, and every validation guard in this program names its own length item the same way, whereas :148-151 name none. CSSETATY's DFHRED and asterisk highlight applies only in the re-enter state AND only where the program actually applies it, and here it does not. The one attribute item the send reports, ERRMSGC, therefore carries the default colour DFHDFCOL; DFHGREEN belongs to the successful-write arm at :727 and to no other. Practice B5 governs: the arm is preserved exactly as written and is not improved by adding a highlight the source does not apply. WHAT THE SEND CARRIES, AND WHY ALL TWENTY-ONE FIELDS ARE PINNED. COTRN2AO REDEFINES COTRN2AI in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY:145, so each xxxI item and its xxxO counterpart occupy the SAME bytes - both sit seven bytes into their field block - and that overlay is why an error path echoes the screen without copying anything. All twenty-one fields carry FSET in app/bms/COTRN02.bms, so the terminal returns all twenty-one and :132 receives all twenty-one; this case declares all twenty-one xxxI items, rather than only the fourteen the program reads, so the echo can actually be asserted. Three outcomes are then distinguishable and all three are pinned: the six header items are REGENERATED by POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 - TRNNAMEO from WS-TRANID, PGMNAMEO from WS-PGMNAME, TITLE01O and TITLE02O from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, and CURDATEO and CURTIMEO from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :554 - so the stale content this case sends up in them is discarded; ERRMSGO is overwritten at :520, so the stale error text is discarded too; and the fourteen operator fields are echoed verbatim at their declared widths. Widths come from PICTURE clauses throughout, per practice B11: the group image is 555 bytes, being twelve bytes of leading FILLER plus twenty-one blocks of seven bytes of xxxL, xxxF and FILLER metadata plus the field itself. STATELESSNESS AND THE COMMAREA (rule R6, gate G37). The conversation travels in the payload and nowhere else - there is no session, so the whole 218 bytes can be read off the response. That 218 is the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy plus the 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO that app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:72-80 declares inside the same 01 group, which sums as sixteen plus sixteen plus eight plus one plus one plus sixteen; the extension stays a separate DTO field and is never folded into the NavigationContext all seventeen online programs share. This arm assigns nothing to either, so all twenty-two fields are pinned to exactly the values they arrived with, including CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT still at '1'. Two of those values are deliberate. The caller is COMEN01C with an admin user type, where case06 arrives from COTRN00C as an ordinary user, which shows that this arm - unlike arm two, whose :137 guard branches on CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM - reads neither field. And CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED arrives NON-blank, which shows that the :124 test against SPACES AND LOW-VALUES belongs to the first-entry branch alone: on re-entry it is never evaluated, so no PROCESS-ENTER-KEY runs, nothing is validated and nothing is written. SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends in EXEC CICS RETURN at :530-534, and a CICS RETURN ends the task, so the send is terminal: exactly one screen, exactly two message images, no second send, and termination is RETURN_TRANSID rather than XCTL. Gate G40 is not asserted here, because this arm performs no XCTL at all. ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION, AND IT STAYS DEAD (practice B5). app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:40 declares WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' and that is the only place the name occurs: the only DATASET operands in the whole program are WS-CXACAIX-FILE at :579, WS-CCXREF-FILE at :612 and WS-TRANSACT-FILE at :645, :676, :705 and :714, so no EXEC CICS command names it. COPY CVACT01Y at :89 is a dead include for the same reason - no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is referenced anywhere, and WS-ACCT-ID-N at :55 is this program's own WORKING-STORAGE while XREF-ACCT-ID comes from CVACT03Y. The translated controller accordingly takes no AccountRepository, so no seeded row could reach it even in principle. This case therefore seeds ACCTDAT from the real 300-byte fixture and pins NOTHING about it - no expectedWrites entry, no expectedFinalState entry and no expectedDatasets entry, here or in any case in this folder - which is the point: the account file is present and populated, and the run still never opens it. Implementing, deleting or tidying the declaration would each be a behaviour change. DATASETS ARE NAMED BY BINDING KEY, NEVER BY DSNAME, so not one of the eight VSAM dataset names app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD binds appears anywhere in this file (gate G46). CCXREF is seeded from fixtures/cardxref.txt at its RAW 36 bytes per record and is deliberately not pre-padded: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares 50 - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) plus XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) plus XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) plus FILLER X(14) - and the fixture omits the trailing FILLER, which is risk R-F. parity/FieldDiffer is the declared sole owner of the 36 to 50 pad and the case declares it as a normalisation rather than performing it, which is gate G16. CXACAIX is not seeded separately, because app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:63-64 defines it as the ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY over the CCXREF base - an alternate-index finder, never a second table (gate G45). No tenth fixture is introduced; AAP 0.4.9 fixes the count at nine. TRANSACT is seeded inline with three 350-byte records and every one of them is pinned unchanged, which is the positive form of the same statement expectedWrites makes negatively: this path writes nothing. GOVERNING PRACTICES: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the entire document, confirmed for this file. No user-specified rule governs it, and their absence is explicitly not treated as licence to lower the bar - AAP 0.10.2's enterprise-practice substitutes bind instead, and the ones this file answers to are B1, no placeholders, so the message is the real literal read out of CSMSG01Y.cpy rather than an invented one; B3, the reference trees are read-only, so that copybook and every other COBOL, BMS, JCL and CSD source was read and never edited; B4, the R-B swap above; B5, the dead ACCTDAT declaration and the unhighlighted arm, both preserved as written; B7, determinism, so the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the instant every case in this folder uses, because :554 reads FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE on every send; B8, explicitness about the chosen AID, the exact literal, its source copybook and the direction of the 80 to 78 move; B11, widths taken from PICTURE clauses and summed rather than assumed; and B12, the honest static-derivation provenance above. The unit is exercised as a plain Java object - the controller is constructed and its handler called directly, with no MockMvc, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). Gates G32, G35, G39 and G43 are deliberately NOT asserted: COTRN02C contains no GO TO at all, no CALL 'CEE3ABD', no pagination on this screen and no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC paragraph.
